title: How is the Bun rewrite in Rust going?
titleZh: Bun 用 Rust 重写的进展如何？
author: tomlockwood
relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: I think it’s important to be very Canny when someone makes a claim that supports a company’s large valuation.
The Bun rewrite seems well positioned as proof-positive that AI and specifically Anthropic’s AI can do the work of open-source maintainers, for some money, but faster.

On the 8th of July 2026 Jarred Summner of Bun fame posted about “Rewriting Bun in Rust”. At the time, I felt pretty Canny, having already read about Anthropic’s C compiler and Cursor’s FastRender web browser. It seems like there is a lot of valuation money riding on the coding capabilities of AI, and a lot of marketing about those capabilities.

It’s not a huge stretch to link the acquisition of Bun by Anthropic with the choice to rewrite Bun with an Anthropic tool. In his article Jarred claims that over 11 days (between 3rd and 14th May 2026) and at a cost of $165,000 for Anthropic API calls the rewrite was done and then merged to main. This represents a cost of $15,000 dollars a day, a cost well outside the means of many open source maintainers. This number doesn’t seem to include the leviathan whirring of the CI/CD in the org’s Buildkite cluster, which appears to have been constantly whirring ever since the “rewrite” was “completed”.
Why do I put those two words in scare quotes?
summaryZh: I think it’s important to be very Canny when someone makes a claim that supports a company’s large valuation.
The Bun rewrite seems well positioned as proof-positive that AI and specifically Anthropic’s AI can do the work of open-source maintainers, for some money, but faster.

comments.author: Jarred
comments.textRawHtml:
Bun’s Rust rewrite shipped in Claude Code over a month ago and barely anyone noticed. Claude Code is widely used. The Rust rewrite is going well overall.

In the Bun v1.4 video, I promised a certain number of newly passing Node.js tests were added to force us to improve compatibility, and that number is not true yet. The release is delayed until it is true. The PRs to make it true are up but not merged yet. Most likely next Tuesday we’ll do the release of 1.4.
comments.textZhHtml:
Bun 的 Rust 重写在一个多月前在 Claude Code 中发布，但几乎没有人注意到。克劳德码被广泛使用。 Rust 重写总体进展顺利。

在 Bun v1.4 视频中，我承诺添加一定数量的新通过的 Node.js 测试来迫使我们提高兼容性，但这个数字还不是真的。发布时间将被推迟，直到消息属实为止。实现这一目标的 PR 已发布，但尚未合并。我们很可能会在下周二发布 1.4。

children.author: inglor
children.textRawHtml:
Take as long as you need to ensure software quality. A month without a release isn't a big deal and whomever needs a specific feature can offer to contribute or build themselves.

Node has 4-6 weeks without a meaningful release (other than security stuff) pretty much every December. I think the criticism in the article is unfounded and whomever needed/wanted a release should have asked first instead of writing an "angry" blog post.

(I'm a Node.js maintainer)
children.textZhHtml:
只要您需要，就可以确保软件质量。一个月没有发布版本并不是什么大问题，任何需要特定功能的人都可以贡献或构建自己。

Node 几乎每年 12 月都会有 4-6 周没有发布有意义的版本（安全性内容除外）。我认为文章中的批评是没有根据的，任何需要/想要发布的人都应该先提出要求，而不是写一篇“愤怒”的博客文章。

（我是 Node.js 维护者）

children.author: inigyou
children.textRawHtml: What is Node getting every 4-6 weeks that makes it noteworthy when it doesn't?
children.textZhHtml: Node 每 4-6 周就会得到什么，这使得它在没有得到的时候值得注意？

children.author: inglor
children.textRawHtml: Text imports (experimental), native addon ESM support, blob textStream(), ReadableStreamTee, byob for readFile, better event loop monitoring and lots of security fixes as well as more minor bug fixes and improvements. (Last 4-6 weeks)
children.textZhHtml: 文本导入（实验性）、原生插件 ESM 支持、blob textStream()、ReadableStreamTee、readFile 的 byob 支持、更好的事件循环监控，以及大量安全修复和更多小错误修复与改进。（过去 4-6 周）

children.author: tomlockwood
children.textRawHtml:
Author here: I don't need or want another Bun release or an NPM release or anything like that. Like I very clearly say in the article I just got chatting with a peer about the Bun rewrite and I decided to take a look.

I'm consistently skeptical about new tech whether it is NoSQL or Blockchain or Serverless. Some of the things I'm skeptical about fail and some succeed.
children.textZhHtml:
作者：我不需要或想要另一个 Bun 版本或 NPM 版本或类似的东西。就像我在文章中非常明确地说的那样，我刚刚与一位同行讨论了 Bun 重写，我决定看一下。

我一直对新技术持怀疑态度，无论是 NoSQL、区块链还是无服务器。有些我怀疑的事情会失败，有些会成功。

children.author: inglor
children.textRawHtml:
The bun Port is a phenomenal engineering achievement that would have taken a team of people over a year or two to deliver previously - look at the TypeScript port for example (and they had llms).

The fact it's taking a while to release is still insanely fast. I'm sure they may be some bumps.

Being skeptical is good and some stuff succeeds and some doesn't - but building tools is still fun and cool, whether it's useful or widely adopted or not :)
children.textZhHtml:
Bun 的移植是一项了不起的工程成就，以前一个团队可能需要一两年才能完成——看看 TypeScript 的移植就知道了（而且他们还有大语言模型辅助）。

虽然发布花了一些时间，但速度依然快得惊人。我相信过程中可能会遇到一些波折。

保持怀疑态度是好事，有些项目成功了，有些则没有——但构建工具依然是一件有趣且很酷的事情，无论它是否有用或是否被广泛采用 :)

children.author: thayne
children.textRawHtml: That's not surprising. Claude code is buggy enough, and releases break things often enough, that I wouldn't expect users to distinguish bugs introduced by switching to rust-based-bun from the normal garden variety bugs.
children.textZhHtml: 这并不奇怪。 Claude 代码有足够多的 bug，而且发布版本经常会破坏一些东西，我不希望用户能够区分通过切换到 rust-based-bun 所引入的 bug 和普通的花园品种 bug。

children.author: AlexErrant
children.textRawHtml:
I can count the number of times an @ file reference doesn't autocomplete on a hundred hands. Or how a rewind won't reset the "is this file Read" marker. Or how a Branch (forking a convo) takes literally 5+secs to run. Or how a slashcommand that's user-only will not work if its in the middle of a prompt. Or how ctrl-r search will match results that don't include any search terms. Or how you can't resume a branch given its session id.

Yes Boris, tell me more about how "coding is solved".

Edit: literally just now, while writing a claude code hook, opus5 gave me this LOC because apparently the changelog and what's in the transcripts _differs_; great docs d00ds.

    # Present only for a subagent's calls. Both spellings accepted: the changelog
    # names `agent_id`, transcripts use `agentId`, and we need not care which lands.
    agent=$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.agent_id // .agentId // empty')
children.textZhHtml:
我可以数出@文件引用没有自动完成的次数一百手。或者倒带如何不会重置“此文件是否已读取”标记。或者一个分支（分叉一个 convo）实际上需要 5 秒以上的时间才能运行。或者，如果用户专用的斜杠命令位于提示符中间，则该命令将无法工作。或者 ctrl-r 搜索如何匹配不包含任何搜索词的结果。或者你如何无法在给定会话 ID 的情况下恢复分支。

是的，鲍里斯，告诉我更多有关“编码是如何解决的”的信息。

编辑：实际上，就在刚才，在编写克劳德代码挂钩时，opus5 给了我这个 LOC，因为显然更改日志和记录中的内容_不同_；很棒的文档 d00ds。

 # 仅适用于子代理的呼叫。两种拼写均被接受：变更日志
    # 名称 `agent_id`，成绩单使用 `agentId`，我们不需要关心是哪个土地。
    agent=$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.agent_id // .agentId // 空')

children.author: maxbond
children.textRawHtml: Claude Code is quite buggy but doesn't generally crash, which is what you would expect if it shipped an immature backend for a month. Maybe the rewrite is full of bugs and they happened to result in the UI glitches or trashed settings files or whatever other application-level bugs that Claude Code has routinely rather than crashes but that would be pretty surprising.
children.textZhHtml: Claude 代码有很多错误，但通常不会崩溃，如果它交付了一个月不成熟的后端，这正是您所期望的。也许重写充满了错误，它们碰巧导致了 UI 故障或设置文件被删除，或者克劳德代码经常出现而不是崩溃的任何其他应用程序级错误，但这将是相当令人惊讶的。
